subject: psychology
title: Biopsychology: Nervous & Endocrine Systems
welcome_lead: Two systems run your body — one fast and electrical, one slow and chemical.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology biopsychology: CNS, PNS, endocrine system, fight or flight.
final_note: Nervous = milliseconds; endocrine = minutes. Both keep you alive.

concepts.def: Central nervous system — brain and spinal cord.
Network of glands releasing hormones into blood.
Hormone from adrenal medulla driving acute stress response.

walkthroughs.body_html: The CNS coordinates: the brain processes, the spinal cord relays. The PNS splits into somatic (voluntary muscles) and autonomic (involuntary organs). The autonomic system further splits into sympathetic and parasympathetic, working in opposition.

The pituitary is the master gland, controlled by the hypothalamus. The adrenal medulla releases adrenaline within seconds; the adrenal cortex releases cortisol over minutes via the HPA axis. Endocrine effects are slower but longer-lasting than nervous signals.

Stress triggers the hypothalamus → sympathomedullary pathway. Adrenaline raises heart rate, dilates pupils, releases glucose, inhibits digestion. After the threat, the parasympathetic branch restores baseline. Taylor (2000) argued women show 'tend and befriend', a critique of male-biased fight-or-flight research.
